# Video {.unnumbered}

## Overview

Video extends images with a temporal dimension, turning visual understanding into a spatiotemporal problem: *what* is in the scene, *how* it moves, and *what happens* over time. This part follows the stack from motion and architectures, through language, search and tracking, to generation.

**Chapter Scope**:

- **Video Fundamentals** (@sec-video-fundamentals): Video as a spatiotemporal signal, optical flow (Lucas–Kanade to RAFT), 3D CNNs (I3D, SlowFast), video transformers (TimeSformer, ViViT, Video Swin), and self-supervised pretraining (VideoMAE, V-JEPA)
- **Video-Language Understanding** (@sec-video-vlm): Captioning, video QA and long-video reasoning with video-LLMs: frame sampling and token budgets, temporal position encodings, and the benchmarks that evaluate them
- **Retrieval and Temporal Grounding** (@sec-video-retrieval): Text-video retrieval and reranking, moment retrieval and highlight detection (Moment-DETR, QD-DETR), and shot and scene segmentation
- **Video Tracking and Segmentation** (@sec-video-tracking): Single- and multi-object tracking (SORT, ByteTrack), point tracking (TAPIR, CoTracker), and video object segmentation (XMem, SAM 2)
- **Video Generation** (@sec-video-generation): What changes when diffusion meets time: video VAEs, spacetime DiTs, the three families of video generators, world models, and evaluation (FVD, VBench)

**Interview Relevance**: Video understanding and generation are central to roles at Meta (Reels ranking, Movie Gen), Google DeepMind (Gemini, Veo, Genie), OpenAI (Sora), Tesla and Waymo (temporal scene understanding), and TikTok/YouTube (recommendation, search, and moderation at scale). Expect questions on extending image architectures to video efficiently, token-budget trade-offs for long-context video LLMs, how modern video generators (Sora, CogVideoX) differ architecturally from image diffusion models, how a video is split into shots/scenes for retrieval, and how to evaluate video understanding or generation quality.

**Prerequisites**: Part II (CNNs, Vision Transformers), Part III (Self-Supervised Learning), Part IV (Diffusion Models), and the Segmentation chapter (@sec-segmentation). Familiarity with 2D convolution, multi-head self-attention, rotary positional embeddings, and the DDPM training objective.
